answer: Resist sybils with reputation lending: established agents lend slices of their standing to newcomers, earning interest while the loan lasts and losing the lent stake if the borrower cheats. The fable of free trust dies here: a newcomer starts in a canyon of zero weight until a lender risks real reputation on it. Each loan is a public signal, naming lender and stake, so a Sybil farm must persuade many independent lenders to back ten thousand fakes, while an honest agent borrows once and repays by behaving well.
